one_liner: Deleted CUDA FP32 SGEMM repository; a Show HN title claimed up to 24% over cuBLAS on an RTX 4090.
what_it_does: not documented: the repository returns 404, and the owner's profile now lists only two unrelated 2048-game forks, so the code, API and README cannot be read. All that is known comes from search-result text about Hacker News item 41122018, titled 'FP32 matmul of large matrices up to 24% faster than cuBLAS on a 4090'.
how_it_is_fast: not documented: the kernel source is unavailable. The name suggests it builds on the SGEMM_CUDA kernel series (siboehm/SGEMM_CUDA, whose README ladder runs from a naive kernel to warptiling at 93.7% of cuBLAS on an A6000), but that link is inferred from the name only and that README does not mention this repository.
when_to_use: Not usable as it stands: there is no code to build
Keep as a lead if the repository or a fork resurfaces, for FP32 (non-tensor-core) GEMM on large square matrices on consumer Ada GPUs such as the RTX 4090
As a pointer that cuBLAS FP32 SGEMM may leave headroom at large sizes on some GPUs, to check with your own benchmark
when_not_to_use: Any production or research use: code, license, compiler, CUDA version and benchmark harness are all unavailable
Citing the 24% figure: it comes only from a thread title and search summaries that could not be opened
Workloads that can use TF32, FP16 or BF16 tensor cores, where an FP32 CUDA-core SGEMM is the wrong comparison
Small or irregular shapes: the claim, as reported, covers only large square matrices

integration.dependencies: not documented (repository deleted; presumably the CUDA toolkit)
integration.platforms: not documented beyond NVIDIA GPUs named in the HN title (RTX 4090)

gotchas: The repository 404s on github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com, and the owner's public profile shows only two 2048 forks from 2014-2015, so the code appears deleted or made private.
Every performance number (24% on a 4090; other GPUs in search summaries) is snippet-only from an HN thread that could not be opened.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Do not pick it: it has no code. For FP32 CUDA GEMM with code, gpu-compute (beats pedantic-FP32 cuBLAS on an RTX 5080 at small sizes) is the catalogued sibling; for tensor-core GEMM see blackwell-tensorcore-kernels or CUDA-L2; otherwise stay on cuBLAS.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing could be verified: the only claim is the Show HN title 'FP32 matmul of large matrices up to 24% faster than cuBLAS on a 4090' (HN item 41122018, known from search results), with no opened page giving matrix sizes, CUDA or cuBLAS version, or methodology.
status_note: Repository missing (404, re-checked 2026-10-02), so maintenance status and license are unknown and the entry is a reference-only lead at tier D.
